pretreatment: sintering (700–800 °C for 2 h) to enhance structural stability, and to provide interconnectivity between the spheres
evidence: The interstitial volume of the opal was next filled with ZnS:Mn using conventional ALD precursors. Etching the infiltrated films in a 2% HF solution resulted in the removal of the silica spheres, and the formation of structurally stable inverse opals. The resulting opal films were polycrystalline, 10mm-thick, 2 cm 32 cm squares, with the (111) planes oriented parallel to the substrate as is typically seen in confinement cell grown opal.
